newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Unions group blasts Indonesia over subversion trial.
newsitem.headline: Unions group blasts Indonesia over subversion trial.

text.p: A major international trades union body blasted Indonesia on Wednesday for putting an independent union leader on trial for subversion.

The International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU) was reacting to news that the subversion trial of Muchtar Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union, would start in Jakarta on Thursday.
"This is just a further attempt by the Indonesian government to muzzle independent trade union activity," the Brussels-based ICFTU said in a statement.
The charge against Pakpahan "is completely without foundation," said the ICFTU, which claims 124 million affiliate members in 136 countries.

"Over the last two years, the government has consistently harassed the independent trade union, including sending army personnel to union headquarters, and arresting its members on trumped up charges and trying them in kangaroo courts," it said.
Pakpahan, accused along with several others on a charge that carries the death penalty, was arrested in connection with riots in Jakarta in July.

At least five people died in the riots, the worst in more than 20 years, which erupted after police raided the headquarters of the opposition Indonesian Democratic Party and evicted supporters of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Pakpahan's lawyer Lutfie Hakim told Reuters on Tuesday that the labour activist was in good health and hoped he would receive a fair trial.
He added that authorities seemed to be preparing to expedite the proceedings and conclude the trial as soon as possible.
"I heard they want to finish the court cases before the general elections," he said.
Indonesia goes to the polls in late May next year.
